introH2: 💑 What kinds of romantic hotel does Chiang Mai have, and how do you pick for two?
introHtml: Chiang Mai slips into a couples trip more easily than you'd think — cool weather in the winter months, an unhurried pace, and a mix of riverside, mountain and old-town settings to wander together · But "romantic" here comes in several shapes, and picking the wrong one changes the whole mood · The first group is resorts on the Ping River that sell quiet garden calm and riverside breakfasts — Na Nirand under a 100-year rain tree, Anantara by Kerry Hill, Cross with its rooftop infinity pool, and the restored teak of 137 Pillars House · The second is design boutiques in the city like Akyra Manor, with an outdoor bathtub on your private balcony and a rooftop infinity pool in the middle of Nimman, or Hotel Yayee, a tiny adults-only place with a rooftop bar facing Doi Suthep · The third is escapes up into the hills for couples who want seclusion — Raya Heritage's artisanal Lanna craft by the river, Four Seasons among the working rice terraces, and Onsen @ Moncham, a mineral-water onsen ryokan on a ridge · The last is old-city boutiques like Rachamankha, classic Lanna beside Wat Phra Singh with the whole walled town on foot · This guide gathers 10 Chiang Mai stays for couples we've reviewed in depth — all built from reading real guest reviews, with the good and the honest caveats spelled out, prices compared across 3 booking sites, and direct links to book
mrtHtml: Chiang Mai has no rail transit, but the city is compact — a Grab or a red songthaew is cheap and easy, and it's only about 10–15 minutes from the airport into town · The couples' stays in this guide are spread across a few zones, and matching the zone to your two-person trip matters more than you'd think · Ping River / Chang Khlan / Wat Ket (near the Night Bazaar) — Na Nirand, Anantara, Cross and 137 Pillars sit here, walkable to the riverside and the Night Bazaar · Nimman — Akyra Manor and Hotel Yayee, with cafés, restaurants and rooftop bars right outside the door · Old City (inside the walls) — Rachamankha, beside Wat Phra Singh, walkable to temples and the walking street · Mae Rim / Hang Dong (30–60 min out of town) — Raya Heritage, Four Seasons and Onsen @ Moncham trade the drive for nature and seclusion · One thing to know: hill stays like Onsen @ Moncham need extra travel time up the mountain, and in March–April Chiang Mai often has burning-season haze — if mountain views are the point, come November–February

entries.addr: 2 Nawatgate Road, Wat Ket, Mueang Chiang Mai
entries.storyHtml: If the point of the trip is "celebrate something special, just the two of us, in a way a brand-new hotel can't deliver," 137 Pillars House is the name that comes up most — a dark-teak house over 130 years old, once a teak-trading office, restored into 30 suites set in a quiet garden by the Ping River in Wat Ket. A member of Small Luxury Hotels of the World, it scores 9.5, the highest of the luxury picks here · Real reviews praise the private-residence feel, a 25-metre pool walled in by planting, service that reads your mind, and a breakfast many call the best they've had in Chiang Mai. Couples who want the most privacy take the Louis Leonowens Pool Suite with its own pool · Honest caveats: rates start around ฿18,000/night and it isn't central — if you plan to be out all day every day, it can feel like an expensive place just to sleep · Best for honeymooners and couples who want to slow down in a quiet heritage setting
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: For the most private couples experience, step up to the Louis Leonowens Pool Suite with its in-room pool · In high season (Nov–Feb) the good suites go fast — book 2+ months ahead and lock a free-cancellation rate · Tell the team if you're celebrating an anniversary or honeymoon so they can arrange a surprise · And don't miss breakfast at Palette

entries.storyHtml: If one Chiang Mai stay was built for couples from the name up, it's Na Nirand Romantic Boutique Resort — turn down a small lane by the Ping River in Chang Khlan and you find a 100-year-old rain tree spreading over the garden, with a Colonial-meets-Lanna building that tells the teak-trade story through teak joinery and hand-woven textiles. Score 9.3 · Real reviews praise the romantic mood under the big tree by the water, the riverside TIME Riverfront restaurant, a breakfast that gets frequent mentions, and free afternoon tea for two — all from around ฿3,900/night, far more accessible than the other riverside luxury names · Honest caveats: the entry-level Deluxe rooms are smallish and don't see the river, and some nights you can hear music from a bar across the water — for the view and quiet, take the Riverfront Colonial Suite and skip weekends · Best for couples and honeymooners who want a riverside mood near the action without paying ultra-luxury rates
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: For a full river view and more space, book the Riverfront Colonial Suite directly and read the room spec first · For total quiet, ask for a room not facing the riverside bar and avoid Fri–Sat · Make the most of the afternoon tea for two · And book ahead for Yi Peng / Loy Krathong, which sells out fast

Score 9.3 · Real reviews praise the private calm of its 33 suites, a roughly 8x20-metre pool running parallel to the river, and the Ai Waan spa with bamboo massage and a herbal steam room. Couples who want an in-room pool take the Kraam Pool Suite · Honest caveats: the Don Kaeo location is out of town, so you rely on a car and lose time if you plan to be in the city daily · Best for couples who want to slow right down by the river, leaning on design, calm and spa over city sightseeing
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: For a private in-room pool, book the Kraam Pool Suite · Reserve Ai Waan spa treatments ahead — few rooms means limited slots · Batch your "into town" days to cut car trips · And in high season, with only 33 suites, book 1–2 months ahead with free cancellation

Step out of the lobby and you're minutes from the Night Bazaar; step back in and it's quiet by the Ping River. Score 9.2 · Real reviews praise the riverside breakfast at Bodhi Terrace, which many call the best in Chiang Mai, afternoon tea in the 1921 House, and service that anticipates. Couples who want an in-room pool take the Lanna Pool Suite · Honest caveats: bathrooms in the entry rooms are on the small side, and street-facing rooms hear some road noise — ask for a river view or higher floor · Best for couples who want understated luxury design, a memorable riverside breakfast, and a walkable location

entries.storyHtml: If the budget stretches and you want a honeymoon in nature you'll remember for life, Four Seasons Resort Chiang Mai is the name couples mention most — a resort in the Mae Rim valley across 32 acres that still grow rice, with pavilions, villas and residences set around green terraces. Couples wanting an in-room pool take a Pool Villa · Honest caveats: it's out of town, a 30–40 minute drive each way, and food and drink inside the resort run noticeably higher than outside · Best for honeymooners and couples marking something special who plan to spend the whole trip inside the resort with nature

entries.storyHtml: For couples who want something novel and private that the city can't offer, Onsen @ Moncham is a Japanese-style ryokan on a ridge near Mon Cham in Mae Rim. The draw is a real natural mineral onsen from the Pong Yaeng source — not a heated tub — and several rooms have their own onsen on the balcony or inside. Score 9.6, the highest in this set · Real reviews describe waking on a 1,200-metre ridge at around 25°C with mist over the fields, soaking in the onsen with the hills in view, plus tatami rooms, Japanese futons and a breakfast that draws praise · Honest caveats: it's nearly an hour out of town, the drive up needs planning, and dining options outside the resort are few; a private onsen is only in certain rooms, so pick the right type · Best for couples who want to escape the city up into the hills, soak together, and let the stay be the whole point of the trip
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: For a private onsen, book an Outdoor Onsen or Imperial Onsen Suite by name before you check out · Allow drive time up the ridge and pack a warm layer — nights are cool · Plan meals in-resort since options outside are few · In high season, with only 24 rooms, the good ones go weeks ahead

advice.head: Love Nimman, cafés and rooftops
advice.bodyHtml: → Akyra Manor ฿3,900, a luxury boutique in central Nimman with an outdoor bathtub + ARISE rooftop bar · or Hotel Yayee ฿1,100, Adults Only with a Doi Suthep rooftop bar — the best value here

advice.head: Want riverside seclusion with design and spa
advice.bodyHtml: → Raya Heritage ฿9,800, an artisanal resort with Lanna craft and the Ai Waan spa · or Anantara Chiang Mai ฿8,500, Kerry Hill design and the Bodhi Terrace riverside breakfast, still walkable to the Night Bazaar

noteHtml: 📌 Note: All prices are approximate starting rates for standard rooms outside peak season and can change by date and season — always check live prices and compare 3 sites before booking · The scores and highlights here come from reading real guest reviews on booking platforms, not from staying ourselves · Chiang Mai's high season (November–February) has the best weather but higher prices and rooms that sell out fast, especially around Yi Peng / Loy Krathong — book 1–2 months ahead · Some stays are adults-oriented (Rachamankha takes no children under 12 · Hotel Yayee is Adults Only) — check the policy before booking if travelling with kids · Out-of-town stays like Four Seasons, Raya Heritage and Onsen @ Moncham are in the Mae Rim / Hang Dong hills, so you rely on a car and should allow drive time up the ridge · In March–April Chiang Mai often has burning-season haze that affects the air and mountain views · Chiang Mai has no rail transit — get around by Grab, red songthaew or hotel transfer · Article by ThailandAddict.com
faqTitle: FAQ — what couples ask most about staying in Chiang Mai

faq.q: ❓ What's the best hotel for couples in Chiang Mai?
faq.a: It depends on your style and budget · For score and luxury, 137 Pillars House at 9.5, restored teak with a pool suite, leads · For a romantic riverside mood at an accessible price, Na Nirand Romantic Boutique Resort at 9.3 was designed for couples · For a special shared experience, Onsen @ Moncham at 9.6, a mountain mineral onsen, or Akyra Manor at 9.3 with its outdoor Nimman bathtub · For a honeymoon with budget in hand, Four Seasons, a rice-terrace resort with 3 MICHELIN Keys

faq.q: ❓ Which romantic stays are on the Ping River?
faq.a: There are several tiers on the Ping · Most accessible and most romantic is Na Nirand at ฿3,900 under a 100-year rain tree · For big rooms and a rooftop infinity pool, Cross Chiang Mai Riverside at ฿4,200, all-suite · For understated design and a riverside breakfast, Anantara at ฿8,500, Kerry Hill design · For heritage, 137 Pillars House at ฿18,000 · For craft-led seclusion, Raya Heritage at ฿9,800 (in Mae Rim, north of town)

faq.q: ❓ Where should we stay for a honeymoon in Chiang Mai?
faq.a: For a full nature honeymoon, Four Seasons Resort Chiang Mai at ฿19,000 — a rice-terrace resort with private Pool Villas and 3 MICHELIN Keys — is the most on-target · For in-town heritage luxury, 137 Pillars House with the Louis Leonowens Pool Suite and its in-room pool · For something novel, a soak together, Onsen @ Moncham up in the hills · Many can arrange a special-occasion surprise — mention it when you book

Yes, and several feel lovely · Hotel Yayee from ฿1,100, an adults-only boutique with a Doi Suthep rooftop bar — the best value here · Na Nirand Romantic Resort from ฿3,900, a romantic riverside resort under the rain tree · Akyra Manor from ฿3,900, a luxury boutique with an outdoor bathtub in Nimman · All three have entry rates in this range, though better-view rooms and suites cost more, and high season pushes rates up

faq.q: ❓ Which have Adults Only, or a private onsen / bathtub?
faq.a: Adults-oriented: Hotel Yayee is fully Adults Only, and Rachamankha takes no children under 12 · For a soak together: Onsen @ Moncham has a private mineral onsen in some rooms (choose Outdoor Onsen / Imperial Onsen Suite) · Akyra Manor has an outdoor balcony bathtub (Premier Suite and up) · And 137 Pillars House, Raya Heritage, Anantara, Cross and Four Seasons have pool suites / pool villas with a private pool

faq.q: ❓ How far ahead should we book, and how do we get around / pick a zone?
faq.a: For Chiang Mai high season (November–February), book 1–2 months ahead, especially around Yi Peng / Loy Krathong when rooms sell out fast; low season needs 2–3 weeks and rates drop · Zones: to walk everywhere, choose the Ping River / Chang Khlan / Wat Ket area (Na Nirand, Anantara, Cross, 137 Pillars), Nimman (Akyra, Yayee) or the Old City (Rachamankha) · For nature and seclusion, Mae Rim / Hang Dong (Raya, Four Seasons, Onsen), but you'll need a car · Chiang Mai has no rail transit — use Grab, red songthaews or hotel transfers · Every platform has free cancellation, so lock a rate if plans are loose, then compare Agoda / Booking / Trip.com for the best price

quickAnswerHtml: 10 Chiang Mai hotels for couples we've reviewed — 137 Pillars House, restored teak with a pool suite (9.5) · Na Nirand Romantic Resort under the rain tree (9.3) · Akyra Manor, outdoor bathtub in Nimman (9.3) · Raya Heritage, artisanal riverside (9.3) · Anantara, Kerry Hill, walk to the Night Bazaar (9.2) · Cross Riverside, all-suite with a rooftop pool (9.2) · Four Seasons, rice terraces, 3 MICHELIN Keys (9.1) · Onsen @ Moncham, a mountain mineral onsen (9.6) · Rachamankha, classic Lanna in the Old City (9.1) · Hotel Yayee, Adults Only with a rooftop bar (9.1) · Honest takes from real reviews, from about ฿1,100–19,000/night, prices compared across 3 sites
